vision_features.image_context: Close-up view of a soybean plant at or near harvest maturity. Multiple stems and seed pods are visible. The plant is photographed at ground level with dark, moist soil and dry plant debris visible in the background. Both stems and attached pods are the primary organs shown.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. Pods: The majority of pods are tan to golden-brown, dry, and papery in texture, consistent with late-season maturation. They are elongated (approximately 30–40 mm long), covered with fine tan-colored hairs, and flattened in appearance, suggesting seeds inside are fully developed or pods are beginning to shrink. Some pods appear incompletely filled — notably flatter and more shrunken than others, distributed throughout the cluster.
2. Stems: The main stems are notably bright green and still appear turgid and living, which contrasts sharply with the dry, brown, dead pods and leaf material. The stems are smooth with fine surface hairs and are approximately 5–8 mm in diameter.
3. Dark spots on stems: At least two distinct small (approximately 2–4 mm), irregular to roughly circular dark brown to black marks are visible on the upper portions of the green stems — one near the top junction and one mid-stem. These marks have no distinct raised texture and appear flat against the stem surface.
4. Leaf and plant tissue: All leaves appear to have dropped or died and dried; only dry, brittle brown fibrous leaf remnants are visible at the base and periphery. No green leaf tissue remains.
5. Pod attachment points (nodes): At several nodes along the stem, clusters of 2–4 pods attach closely together. The node tissue appears slightly darkened or discolored (dark brown to near-black) at a few attachment points, contrasting with the otherwise green stem.
vision_features.absences:
1. No visible powdery or dusty coating on any surface — stems and pods appear clean.
2. No visible raised pustules, tiny black dots embedded within lesions, or thread-like surface growths on the pods or stems.
3. No yellowing (green-to-yellow transition tissue) is present — the transition is directly from green stems to fully brown/dead pods and debris, with no intermediate yellow tissue.
4. No visible exudate, slime, or wet rot on any part of the plant.
vision_features.summary: The image shows a soybean plant at late maturity with green, still-living stems bearing clusters of dry, tan-brown, hairy seed pods that are mostly fully matured and some appearing underfilled or shrunken. All leaf tissue has senesced and fallen, leaving only dry brown debris. The most striking visual contrast is the persistence of fully green, turgid stems while all pods and leaves are completely dry and brown. Small dark brown to black flat marks are present at two or more points on the green stems, most notably near node attachment areas. The pods are the most visually affected organs in terms of senescence, though the stem discoloration marks are the most unusual feature.

────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold covering; seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on stem near soil line.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered; symptoms usually begin in the upper canopy on young leaves.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur..
